input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle guard (`seen` set of exception ids) was removed from the `__cause__` traversal loop. A circular `__cause__` chain now makes the `while exc is not None` loop run forever.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception whose `__cause__` chain loops back on itself (e.g. `a.__cause__ = b; b.__cause__ = a`, or `e.__cause__ = e`), with none of the exceptions matching `exception_cause_types`. Mechanism: no visited check remains, so `exc = exc.__cause__` cycles indefinitely. Impact: the retry predicate hangs, which blocks the retrying call. Python does not forbid such cycles when `__cause__` is assigned manually.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: the __cause__ traversal has no cycle guard, so a self-referential or mutually-causing chain makes the loop run forever and the retry predicate hangs. Same operation, same failure.
